strengths: Novel core insight: GHNs with CNN decoders structurally align weight spaces, enabling patch-based width-agnostic generation. Figure 3 provides compelling visual evidence.
Addresses a real limitation of prior methods that couple generation to fixed matrix dimensions, enabling practical benefits for hardware-constrained deployment.
Strong empirical results: >85% success on unseen topologies while baselines degrade to 59-42%, demonstrating genuine generalization rather than memorization.

Comprehensive experimental validation within scope: ablations show alignment without mode collapse (Table 1, 6), clear seen/unseen separation (Table 2), joint generation capability (Table 3), and diversity analysis.
Rigorous evaluation domain: robotic manipulation is a strict metric where small weight errors cause failure, unlike vision tasks; direct deployment in ManiSkill3.
Clear presentation: well-written with intuitive multimodal tokenization scheme (discrete architecture tokens + continuous weight patches), logical flow, and good visualizations.
Solid technical execution: the MoNL framework adaptation for dual-modality generation is well-implemented with appropriate conditioning schemes.
weaknesses: Severely limited experimental scope undermines generality claims: only 4-layer MLPs tested (acknowledged in Section 7 as computational constraint), only {16, 32, 64} width vocabulary, only 3 simple robotic tasks, no other architecture classes (CNNs, Transformers).

Core contribution rests on empirical observation without theoretical justification: why specifically do CNN decoders induce locality bias? No ablation on decoder architecture (MLP vs Transformer decoders). Mechanism is stated but not rigorously explained.

Circular dependency in dataset construction: training data generated entirely by GHNs (128 GHNs, top-100 per arch), then NNiT learns GHN-conditioned distribution. Model doesn't learn to generate arbitrary MLPs but rather GHN-compatible ones.

Baseline comparisons lack fairness: SANE fails dramatically (1% on training set) but no ablation validates explanation; D2NWG retains 89% on PushCube unseen widths (attributed to task simplicity without deeper investigation); no methods target width-agnostic generation so adapted baselines aren't purpose-built.

Critical technical details underspecified: patch size p never explicitly stated, weight extraction/cropping mechanism for varying widths not detailed, decoder architecture referenced externally, no sensitivity analysis for key hyperparameters.

Experimental design issues: top-10 selection from 100 samples introduces selection bias; MoNL 50-50 joint/conditional ratio unjustified with no ablation; small test set (8/72 architectures); comparison to just training small networks directly not provided.
Missing ablation studies: no ablation on patch size p, MoNL ratio, GHN vs alternative hypernetwork designs, or CNN decoder architecture choices—these are essential for validating design decisions.

Insufficient practical utility analysis: generating policies is niche; training time for generative model not reported; inference requires sampling 100 policies; unclear when this beats direct training of small networks.

Theoretical grounding weak: permutation symmetry proof (Eq. 1) is standard; connection between structural alignment and patchification underexplored; why alignment enables patchification deserves formal treatment.
Reproducibility concerns: no code release mentioned, some hyperparameters scattered across appendix, GHN details referenced externally, patch size p left unspecified in main text.

strengths: Novel contribution addressing genuine limitation: Width-agnostic weight generation overcomes the fixed-dimensional coupling problem of prior vectorization-based methods (SANE, D2NWG)

Strong empirical insight and validation: GHNs with CNN decoders demonstrably induce structural alignment (r≈0.65 cross-seed correlation, Figure 3) without mode collapse (L2 distance 54.66), with permutation ablation proving necessity
Convincing zero-shot transfer results: >85% success on unseen architectures vs. 1-59% for baselines; NNiT's worst-case (64.8%) exceeds D2NWG's mean (15.6%)
Comprehensive experimental suite: Multiple robotic tasks, MNIST validation, extensive ablations including CKA analysis, diversity metrics, and deployment pipeline

Genuine technical innovation: Multimodal joint architecture-weight generation p(a,w) is novel and achieves 99-100% success; patch-based tokenization elegantly decouples generation from fixed dimensions
Methodologically sound: Mixture of Noise Levels adaptation for dual-modality conditioning is clean; experimental design appropriately tests main claims
Honest limitations discussion: Clearly acknowledges 4-layer restriction and proposes stabilization techniques for deeper networks rather than overclaiming scalability
weaknesses: Severely limited experimental scope: Restricted to 4-layer MLPs (acknowledged computational limitation but undermines generality claims); vocabulary only {16,32,64}; only 3 robotic tasks; insufficient to support broad width-agnostic claims

Problematic circular dependency on GHNs: Requires task-specific GHN training first (128 GHNs, 500-1500 iterations); no computational cost comparison to SGD; generalization tested only on ManiSkill3 variants, not truly different domains
Overclaimed width-agnosticism: Model only handles widths within training vocabulary; cannot generate arbitrary widths; padding strategy (H×W grid) limits maximum width; more accurate framing needed

Baseline comparison fairness concerns: SANE's 1% success seems suspiciously poor with limited justification for adaptation fairness; D2NWG designed for fixed architectures; missing comparisons with recent cited generative models (Liang et al. 2024, Saragih et al. 2025)

Insufficient structural alignment explanation: Claim that GHNs 'collapse permutation symmetries' stated but not formally proven; no ablation comparing CNN vs. other decoder architectures; locality bias explanation is intuitive but not theoretically justified

Methodology limitations: Top-10 selection metric (generating 100, selecting 10) is artificial—practical deployment needs high single-sample success rates; suspiciously high joint generation rates (99-100%) raise questions whether model learned training distribution rather than true generation; custom StackCubeEasy-v1 task appears engineered for stability

Reproducibility and practical concerns: No code/data release; training cost not reported; dataset filtering is task-specific; MNIST evaluation downsamples 784→32 via PCA; promised meta-learning and hardware optimization applications mentioned but never demonstrated

Missing technical details and ablations: No study of patch size effects; no analysis of vocabulary size sensitivity; asymmetry between depth and width transfer not discussed; MoNL framework details relegated to appendix; interaction between architecture tokens and weight patches in self-attention unclear
